seo.title: YouTube Thumbnail Maker – 1280×720 Bold-Text Thumbnails
seo.description: Describe your video and headline, add your photo if you like, and get a YouTube thumbnail at exactly 1280×720 px, under 2 MB and ready to upload.
intro: Tell PiCraft what the video is about and the words you want on the thumbnail. It designs a high-contrast image with one clear focal point that stays readable on a phone.
Add a photo of yourself or your product to put it front and center. The file comes out at 1280×720 px and under 2 MB, small enough to upload from the YouTube app or a computer.

prompt:
Design a YouTube video thumbnail, 16:9 landscape, for a video about: {{topic}}
Visual style: {{style}}.
Large, bold, highly legible headline text reading exactly "{{headline}}", spelled exactly as written, at most two lines, placed in the left or right third with strong contrast against the background.
[[Feature the person or product from {{photo}} prominently with an expressive, attention-grabbing pose or angle, keeping their face and identity exactly the same.]]
One clear focal point that reads instantly on a small phone screen. Keep text and faces away from the bottom-right corner, where YouTube shows the video length. No other text, no YouTube logo, no watermark.

specs.heading: YouTube thumbnail requirements
rows: As large as possible; YouTube recommends 3840×2160 px, and 1280×720 px is a common working size
2 MB when uploading from mobile, 50 MB from a computer
notes: PiCraft's 1280×720 px file stays under 2 MB, so it uploads from mobile and desktop. The 1920×1080 px file can be larger than 2 MB, so upload it from a computer.
YouTube overlays the video length in the bottom-right corner, so PiCraft keeps text and faces out of that area.
Custom thumbnails require a verified YouTube account.

faq.q: Is the thumbnail the right size?
faq.a: The main file is 1280×720 px, 16:9, as a JPG under 2 MB. YouTube recommends uploading the largest 16:9 image you can, with a minimum width of 640 px and a 2 MB limit when you upload from mobile. The 1920×1080 px version gives you more resolution for uploads from a computer.

faq.q: Can I use my own face?
faq.a: Yes. Upload a clear photo and the design features you prominently while keeping your likeness.

faq.q: How long should the text be?
faq.a: 2–5 words is ideal. Long sentences become unreadable at the size thumbnails appear in search and suggested videos.

faq.q: Can I make thumbnails for Shorts?
faq.a: This maker creates 16:9 thumbnails for regular videos. YouTube recommends a vertical 9:16 image for Shorts thumbnails, which you add in YouTube Studio on a computer, so this maker is not the right tool for them.

faq.q: Do I need a verified YouTube account?
faq.a: Yes. YouTube only allows custom thumbnails on verified accounts. If the option is missing in YouTube Studio, verify your account first.

faq.q: Why is the bottom-right corner empty?
faq.a: YouTube shows the video length there, and it would cover any text or face placed in that corner, so the design keeps it clear.

faq.q: How do I upload the thumbnail?
faq.a: In YouTube Studio, open Content, choose the video, and under Thumbnail click Upload file. Pick the downloaded JPG and save.
Yes. Generate a few versions of the same video and try them one at a time, giving each enough time to collect views before you compare.

faq.q: Can I use someone else's photo?
faq.a: Only with their permission. Use photos of yourself, your team or products you own, and don't upload pictures of other people without their consent.

faq.q: Will the thumbnail look like me?
faq.a: Usually it keeps your likeness, but AI can alter small features. Check your face closely and generate again if it looks off.
